title: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension: Adaptive Damping
introduction: I separate the spring’s job from the damper’s job: the spring supports the load and stores energy, while the damper resists motion and helps it settle. Think of a door closer controlling a swinging door. This suspension makes that motion control adjustable as road and driving conditions change. This is a system overview, with no inspection, adjustment or replacement procedure.

edits.text: The semi-active, computer-controlled suspension damping system uses vehicle sensors and magneto-rheological fluid-filled dampers. It continuously adjusts adaptive shock absorber force to suit the current road and driving conditions, helping improve handling, comfort and stability.
edits.why: The adjustable quantity is damping force—the resistance that controls suspension movement. I read “adaptive” as ongoing adjustment to conditions, rather than one fixed damping setting for every stretch of road. The spring still has its separate load-supporting role.
